text:
omar: hi all, first-day hiccup. trying to push to git@github.com:redwood/rl-serving.git and getting `remote: Repository not found.` Browser shows 403 with a banner that SAML SSO is required. i accepted the org invite but still blocked.
it-ops: welcome! quick checks: which email did you accept with, and are you using SSH or HTTPS? also `ssh -T git@github.com` output helps.
omar: accepted with omar.temp@gmail.com originally, then team resent to omar@redwood.com. using SSH. `ssh -T git@github.com` -> `Hi omarold! You've successfully authenticated, but GitHub does not provide shell access.`
hera: looks like your ssh key is attached to your personal account. if you added the same key to the org as a deploy key on any repo, GitHub treats it repo-scoped and won't map it to your user. try `ssh-add -l` and check key fingerprints.
omar: `ssh-add -l` shows one key. fingerprint `SHA256:ZqFakeFingerPrint987`.
scim-bot: SCIM: user omar@redwood.com provisioned -> teams: models, serving (2025-11-04T14:09:02Z).
it-ops: can you paste the public key (only .pub) or the fingerprint and i'll check deploy keys quickly.
omar: here's pub: `ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIMockedKeyForOmar omar@redwood.com`
hera: that fingerprint matches a deploy key on docs.redwood (read-only). deploy key parents block the key from being used as a user SSH key. add a new key to your user account or we'll reassign. Also make sure you clicked the org "Authorize SSO" button after you accepted the invite; SAML must be authorized to grant repo access.
omar: i see the authorize button now under Profile -> Organizations -> Redwood Inference, clicked it and connected Okta.
it-ops: after SSO auth you may need to refresh GH CLI/token state. `gh auth status` and `gh auth refresh -h github.com` can help. If you created a PAT before SSO it won't be valid for org repos.
omar: `gh auth status` shows logged in as omarold. ran `gh auth logout` then `gh auth login --web` and chose omar@redwood.com.
omar: added new key ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_redwood and added the pub to my profile. `ssh -T git@github.com` -> `Hi omar! You've successfully authenticated, but GitHub does not provide shell access.`
hera: good. I also triggered a SCIM reprovision and checked team assignments; you should have the repo-level grant. scim-bot: "SCIM: reprovision triggered for omar@redwood.com (jobs queued)"
omar: trying clone now... still `Repository not found` for rl-serving but other repos clone fine.
it-ops: that suggests fine-grained repo permissions or team grant lag on that specific repo. i just added you directly to the repo's access list and invited the team. you should get an email.
omar: got the invite and accepted, clone succeeded. push also works now. thanks! :tada:
hera: follow-up notes: 1) prefer sending invites to redwood.com emails only, 2) add an onboarding step to explicitly authorize SSO before generating PATs, 3) avoid reusing an SSH key as a deploy key + user key. i'll add these to the onboarding checklist.
it-ops: filing onboarding ticket ONB-3819 to update docs and add a small troubleshooting snippet for `ssh-add`, `gh auth refresh`, and how to spot deploy-key conflicts. welcome aboard, @omar :wave:
